ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r1.claim: Sūrah al-Layl pairs with al-Shams; their central themes and inner and outer features correspond so closely that even a general reader can sense the harmony.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r1.anchor: There is no essential difference between the central themes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.claim: Al-Layl develops the preceding sūrah’s claim that the soul succeeds through purification by identifying what corrupts it and how it can be protected and purified.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.anchor: the things which contaminate it are explained

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r3.claim: Verses 1–4 use evidence from the outer and inner worlds to establish that Judgment must come: the Hereafter is this world’s counterpart and makes it meaningful.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r3.anchor: The evidence of the world around man and the world within him is presented to show that the Day of Judgement is bound to come.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p345/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p345/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p345/r1.claim: Oaths by natural phenomena in the Qur’an are intended to establish a premise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p345/r1.anchor: the various oaths sworn by natural phenomena are meant to substantiate a

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r1.claim: Night and day, like male and female, are complementary pairs whose members fill one another’s void and together serve their created purpose; without a counterpart, their capacities and uses make no sense.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r1.anchor: the male and female species form complementary pairs and together these pairs fulfil the purpose for which they have been created

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r2.claim: The harmony of opposites argues for monotheism and, here, for the Hereafter; 51:49 calls pairs a reminder that this world has a counterpart completing its purpose.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, and Ibn ʿĀmir open the endings in this sūrah, al-Layl, and al-Ḍuḥā.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر: بفتح أواخر آي هذه السورة

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r2.speaker: الكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī uses imālah throughout these endings and the endings of al-Layl and al-Ḍuḥā.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r2.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي بإضجاع ذلك كله، وإضجاع أواخر سورة والليل

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r4.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ has several transmissions: some make the endings intermediate, while Warsh and Qālūn are also reported to open them all; another report opens only talāhā and inclines the rest.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع ذلك كله بين الفتح والكسر. وقال خلف عن إسحاق

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr is reported as using intermediate imālah, while ʿAbbās reports fully inclined forms for selected endings; other transmissions describe his treatment across verse endings.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p418/r5.anchor: وقال اليزيدي عن أبي عمرو: ذلك كله بين الفتح والكسر

TUSTARI:92:1/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:1/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:92:1/r1.claim: Inwardly, the night signifies the natural self.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the case of إذا is problematic: coordination either makes the wāws govern both accusative and genitive, or oath wāws create a disputed construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r2.anchor: فإن قلت: الأمر في نصب إذا معضل، لأنك إما أن تجعل الواوات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r3.claim: The author rejects treating coordinating wāws as governors; the governing case comes from the element governing the first conjunct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r3.anchor: أما قوله في واوات العطف فتنصب بها وتجر فليس هذا بالمختار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r4.claim: This is coordination of two genitive and accusative pairs, not coordination under two separate governors; he gives مررت بزيد أمس وعمرو اليوم as the parallel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r4.anchor: ليس ما في الآية من العطف على عاملين، وإنما هو من باب عطف اسمين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r5.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r5.claim: Sibawayh's poetic example coordinates a genitive and nominative with the same case pattern, supporting the author's construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r5.anchor: وقد أنشد سيبويه في كتابه: فليس بمعروف لنا أن نردها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r6.speaker: الخليل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r6.claim: Al-Khalīl says the last two wāws join nouns like ordinary coordination, while the first is like the prepositional bāʾ and tāʾ of oath.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r6.anchor: قال الخليل: في قوله عز وجل: والليل إذا يغشى والنهار إذا تجلى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r7.claim: The author says al-Khalīl's statement indicates prohibition, contrary to al-Zamakhsharī's claim that the construction is merely disliked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p487/r7.anchor: وأما قوله على استكراه فليس كما ذكر، بل كلام الخليل يدل على المنع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan according to the author, Madinan according to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, with another report that some of it is Madinan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية. وقال علي بن أبي طلحة: مدنية. وقيل: فيها مدني.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.claim: The surah explains which traits bring the success and failure just mentioned in the previous surah, then warns of the Fire and distinguishes those entering it from those spared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها ، ذكر هنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r3.claim: The object of يغشى is omitted and may be the day, the sun, or the earth and all it contains under darkness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r3.anchor: ومفعول يغشى محذوف، فاحتمل أن يكون النهار، كقوله: يغشي الليل النهار ،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r5.claim: The oaths evoke the night when living creatures take shelter and the day when they spread out.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r5.anchor: أقسم بالليل الذي فيه كل حيوان يأوي إلى مأواه، وبالنهار الذي تنتشر فيه.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p147/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p147/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p147/r1.claim: The night may cover the sun, the day, or whatever it veils in general; on every reading, the sworn object is the whole night.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p147/r1.anchor: أي حين يغشى الشمس كقوله تعالى والليل إذا يغشاها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r1.claim: Night covers day with darkness and removes its light.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r1.anchor: {والليل إذا يغشى} أي يغشى النهار بظلمة فيذهب بضوئه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r1.claim: Night veils the sun, day, or everything its darkness hides.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r1.anchor: { واليل إذا يغشى } أي يغشى الشمس أو النهار أو كل ما يواريه بظلامه

BINTSHATI:v2p98/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r1.claim: The root gh-sh-y means covering; its derivatives describe a veil, dulling of perception in sleep or fainting, and the covering of sight or insight.
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r1.anchor: ومن غشية النعاس المعطلة للحس والإدراك، جاءت غشية الإغماء

BINTSHATI:v2p98/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r2.claim: The Quran uses covering for rejection in Noah 71:7 and Hud 11:5, for the overwhelming manifestation at the lote tree, and for sleep, fainting, or a veil over heart and senses.
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r2.anchor: وفي الاستعمال القرآني، جاءت الغاشية على معناها في استغشاء الثياب حاجزاً دون السمع والبصر

BINTSHATI:v2p98/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r3.claim: The root often describes the Day of Judgment and its punishments covering people, faces, or places.
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r3.anchor: وكثر مجئ الغشية في الحديث عن يوم القيامة

BINTSHATI:v2p98/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r4.claim: The root can name terrors or darkness; the author understands night in this surah as a covering of deep darkness.
BINTSHATI:v2p98/r4.anchor: والغواشي الأهوال، أو الظلمات تلقى لفاعها الأسود

BINTSHATI:v2p99/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p99/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p99/r1.claim: The word tajalli means appearing or becoming uncovered; its physical senses include recession of the hairline, polish that clears sight, display of a bride, and polishing a blade or mirror.

BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.claim: The oath's night, daylight, and creation frame divergent earthly endeavors, then contrasting afterlife fates: the denier's fire and the pious giver's satisfaction.
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا النسق من البيان المعجز، يتم الربط بين المقسم به في أول السورة:

BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#s092/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#s092/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#s092/r1.claim: The surah demonstrates God’s complete, freely chosen governance of souls through people’s divergent efforts despite sharing aims.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#s092/r1.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على مقصود الشمس ، وهو التصرف التام في النفوس بإثبات كمال القدرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#s092/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#s092/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#s092/r2.claim: Its name, al-Layl, signals that night frustrates ordinary desire through darkness and sleep, the sibling of death.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#s092/r2.anchor: ليل نفسه دال على ذلك لأنه على غير مراد النفس بما فيه من الظلام والنوم الذي هو أخو الموت

BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r1.claim: After the preceding surah’s account of purified and corrupted souls and Thamud’s fate, people diverge between good and evil while God governs souls through piety and wickedness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r1.anchor: لما بين في الشمس حال من زكى نفسه وحال من دساها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r2.claim: Night signifies confusion and obscurity, gradually covering what daylight made visible; it is suited to secrecy.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r2.anchor: أي يغطي ما كان من الوجود مبصرا بضياء النهار على التدريج قليلا قليلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r4.claim: Those seeking secrecy choose night and those seeking publicity choose day, whether righteous or wicked.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r4.anchor: فمن كان يريد السر قصد الليل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r3.claim: Some interpreters say spiritual light from night prayer and other good deeds will bring sensory light after death.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن المراد بالتجلي بالنور المعنوي من إنارة ظلام الليل

NAHHAS:v5p241/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p241/r1.claim: The object of yaghshā is omitted either because the listener knows it or to leave it vague; the night covers everything in darkness like a garment, unlike the day.
NAHHAS:v5p241/r1.anchor: حذف المفعول كما يقال ضرب زيد ولا يجيء بالمضروب إما لمعرفة السامع وإما أن تريد أن تبهم عليه قيل المعنى والليل إذا يغشى كل شيء بظلمته فيصير له كالغشاء وليس كذا النهار

NAHHAS:v5p241/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r2.speaker: النابغة الذبياني
NAHHAS:v5p241/r2.claim: His poem compares night to a pursuer who catches the speaker even when escape seems far away.

DURR-FULL:v8p497/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r2.claim: The Prophet rebuked Muadh for overlong prayer and directed him to recite shorter chapters, including the chapters beginning with glorification, the sun, dawn, and night.

DURR-FULL:v8p527/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r5.claim: The Prophet told him to recite both the Night and the Sun surahs in the dawn prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r5.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أمره

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas links the sura's revelation to a sale: a stingy palm owner deprived a poor household of fallen dates, then a believer traded forty palms for the tree and gave it to the family; the buyer received a promised palm in Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ان رجلا كان له نخل ومنها نخلة فرعها إلى دار رجل صالح فقير ذي عيال

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses the night as coming and covering everything.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير والليل اذا يغشى قال : اذا اقبل فغطى كل شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r2.claim: The object of يغشى is omitted because the verb functions intransitively: the lesson is that night covers everything in darkness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r2.anchor: وحذف مفعول { يغشى } لتنزيل الفعل منزلة اللازم لأن العبرة بغشيانه كل ما تغشاه ظلمته .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r4.claim: The passage alludes to night darkness as the original state of the solar system and daylight as following the sun's creation; time reckoning accordingly began with nights before days.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r4.anchor: وأشير إلى أن ظلمة الليل كانت غالبة لضوء النهار وأن النهار يعقبها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r5.claim: The time restrictions on night and day follow the explanation of their corresponding oaths in the preceding surah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r5.anchor: والقول في تقييد الليل بالظرف وتقييد النهار بمثله كالقول في قوله : { والنهار إذا جلاها والليل إذا يغشاها في السورة السابقة } ( الشمس : 3 ، 4 ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r5.speaker: علقمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r5.claim: In a report in both Ṣaḥīḥs, Abū al-Dardāʾ asks how Ibn Masʿūd recited the oath; ʿAlqama gives the wording with الذكر والأنثى, and Abū al-Dardāʾ says he heard the Prophet recite it so.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r5.anchor: عن علقمة قال : ( دخلت في نفر من أصحاب عبد الله ( يعني ابن مسعود ) الشام فسمع بنا أبو الدرداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls this the Prophet's reading; Ibn ʿĀshūr explains it as an early permitted variant that was later replaced by the final reading agreed upon by the reciters and written in Abū Bakr's muṣḥaf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r6.anchor: وتأويل ذلك : أنه أقرأها أبا الدرداء أيام كان القرآن مرخصا فيه أن يقرأ على بعض اختلاف ، ثم نسخ ذلك الترخيص

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p145#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p145#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p145#2/r1.claim: Night covers the day with its darkness.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p145#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p145#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p145#2/r2.claim: Night covers the horizon and everything between heaven and earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p145#2/r2.anchor: يغشى الأفق ويغشى جميع ما بين السماء والأرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p416#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p416#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p416#2/r3.claim: The night oath refers to darkness covering creation and the day oath to its light and brightness; the paired created male and female recalls other creation pairs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p416#2/r3.anchor: أي: إذا غشي الخليقة بظلامه، {والنهار إذا تجلى} أي: بضيائه وإشراقه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that a palm owner repeatedly snatched fruit from poor children in a neighbor's house; the Prophet offered him a palm in Paradise, but he refused, so another man exchanged forty palms for it and donated it to the family.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r1.anchor: أن رجلا كان له نخل، ومنها نخلة فرعها إلى (7) دار رجل صالح فقير ذي عيال،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the story of the palm and the charitable buyer occasioned the revelation of the surah's opening through its contrast between giving and withholding.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r2.anchor: قال عكرمة: قال ابن عباس: فأنزل الله عز وجل: {والليل إذا يغشى} إلى قوله:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the palm-story report transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim very unusual.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r1.anchor: هكذا رواه ابن أبي حاتم، وهو حديث غريب جدا.

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r1.speaker: أبي
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet promises that reciters of Sūrat al-Layl will receive until contentment, be protected from hardship, and have ease made easy for them.
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r1.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (والليل) أعطاه الله حتي يرضى

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r2.claim: Following the previous chapter's account of the believer and disbeliever and their outcomes, this chapter gives the same contrast again.
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r2.anchor: ولما تقدم في السورة المتقدمة بيان حال المؤمن والكافر، وما فعل بهما، أتبعه بمثل ذلك

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r4.claim: Ghishāʾ means covering or veiling, and tajallī means illumination and clarity.
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r4.anchor: أصل الغشاء: الستر، ومنه: الغاشية والغشيان. والتجلي: الإنارة والوضوح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766/r1.claim: What the night covers may be the sun, by reference to 91:4; the day, by reference to 13:3; or everything hidden by its darkness, by reference to 113:3.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766/r1.anchor: المغشي : إما الشمس من قوله : { واليل إذا يغشاها } ( الشمس : 4 ) وإما النهار

MAWARDI:92:1/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:1/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:1/r1.claim: The sūra of al-Layl is Meccan by consensus.

MAWARDI:92:1/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:1/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:92:1/r2.claim: Mujahid explains the night phrase as meaning when the night darkens.

MAWARDI:92:1/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:1/r3.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI:92:1/r3.claim: Ibn Jubayr explains the night phrase as meaning when it covers and conceals.

MAWARDI:92:1/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:1/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:92:1/r4.claim: Qatada explains it as the night covering all creatures, encompassing and filling them.
MAWARDI:92:1/r4.anchor: إذا غشى الخلائق فعّمهم وملأهم ، قاله قتادة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r1.claim: The unexpressed object of 'covers' is understood from context; one possibility is the sun mentioned in the earlier oath.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r1.anchor: المغشى اما الشمس من قوله والليل إذا يغشاها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r2.claim: Another possibility is that night covers the day, as stated in the verse about night and day covering one another.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r2.anchor: أو النهار من قوله يغشى الليل النهار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r3.claim: Another possibility is that night covers everything it veils with darkness, as in the verse about nightfall.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#2/r3.anchor: أو كل شئ يواريه بظلامه من قوله إذا وقب

QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r1.claim: Yaghshā means covers; the object is omitted because it is understood.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والليل إذا يغشى } أي يغطي. ولم يذكر معه مفعولا للعلم به.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r2.claim: Possible objects are the day, earth, creatures, or everything with its darkness.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r2.anchor: وقيل: يغشى النهار. وقيل: الأرض. وقيل: الخلائق. وقيل: يغشى كل شيء بظلمته.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r3.speaker: قتادة عن سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r3.claim: God first created light and darkness, then distinguished them as dark night and bright, seeing day.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:2-3/r3.anchor: وروى سعيد عن قتادة قال: أول ما خلق الله النور والظلمة، ثم ميز بينهما

QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r1.claim: The surah sets the varied human work and its differing recompense in a cosmic frame; its two opposed human outcomes match the contrasts of night and day and of male and female.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r1.anchor: في إطار من مشاهد الكون وطبيعة الإنسان تقرر السورة حقيقة العمل والجزاء

QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r2.claim: Night covers, envelops, and hides the world, while day appears, reveals, and makes things plain; they oppose one another in the cycle, appearance, qualities, and effects.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r2.anchor: الليل حين يغشى البسيطة ، ويغمرها ويخفيها . والنهار حين يتجلى ويظهر

QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r3.claim: The broad alternation of night and day affects the soul directly and evokes the mysterious universe, human inability to control it, change, and a power directing the cosmos.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r3.anchor: ولهذا التقلب حديث وإيحاء . حديث عن هذا الكون المجهول الأسرار

QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r4.claim: Their regular, precise order proves another hand directs the heavens; the one governing the cosmos also directs human lives and did not create people purposelessly.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r4.anchor: بهذا الانتظام وهذا الاطراد وهذه الدقة . وأن الذي يدير الفلك هكذا يدير حياة البشر أيضا

QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r5.claim: Even amid deniers’ attempts to divert attention, the human heart remains connected to the universe and instinctively recognizes its director, as well as through reflection.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:1/r5.anchor: ويدرك تلقائيا كما يدرك بعد التدبر والتفكر ، أن هنالك مدبرا

RAZI-FULL:v31p179#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p179#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p179#2/r1.claim: Night shelters animals, stills creatures and brings restorative sleep; day removes darkness and sets people, birds and other creatures moving for livelihood. Their alternation serves both work and rest, as 25:62 and 14:33 say.

RAZI-FULL:v31p179#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p179#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p179#2/r2.claim: The omitted object of 'covers' may be the sun, the day, or anything concealed by darkness, as in 91:4, 13:3 and 113:3.

STUDYQURAN:92:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:intro/r1.claim: Al-Layl is early Makkan and often considered ninth in revelation order, though some call it Madinan or partly Madinan; it is named after the opening oath.
STUDYQURAN:92:intro/r1.anchor: often considered the ninth in the chronological order of revelation

STUDYQURAN:92:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:intro/r2.claim: The first three verses echo the prior surah's polarity; the rest stresses diverse human ends and the opposed outcomes of good and evil deeds.
STUDYQURAN:92:intro/r2.anchor: Similar to the first ten verses of the preceding sūrah, the first three verses of this sūrah focus upon the polarity inherent to the created order

STUDYQURAN:92:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r1.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r1.claim: The omitted object of “enshrouds” may be the world.
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r1.anchor: The omitted direct object can be seen as an allusion to the world, the earth, the day

STUDYQURAN:92:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r2.claim: The omitted object may be the earth.
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r2.anchor: The omitted direct object can be seen as an allusion to the world, the earth, the day

STUDYQURAN:92:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r3.claim: The omitted object may be the day.
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r3.anchor: The omitted direct object can be seen as an allusion to the world, the earth, the day

STUDYQURAN:92:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r4.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r4.claim: The omitted object may be all of creation.
STUDYQURAN:92:1/r4.anchor: The omitted direct object can be seen as an allusion to the world, the earth, the day

TAB-FULL:v24p455#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p455#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p455#2/r1.claim: The night veils the day with darkness and removes its light; the day then clears, shines, and makes visible what night concealed.
TAB-FULL:v24p455#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله {والليل إذا يغشى والنهار إذا تجلى} [الليل: 2] قال: آيتان عظيمتان يكورهما الله

TAB-FULL:v24p455#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p455#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p455#2/r2.claim: Qatadah calls night and day two great signs that God rotates over creation.
TAB-FULL:v24p455#2/r2.anchor: آيتان عظيمتان يكورهما الله على الخلائق

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-3:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-3:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-3:anmerkung/r1.claim: Qur'anic oaths probably draw on a characteristic expression of pre-Islamic soothsayers, a connection not yet sufficiently studied.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-3:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu grundsätzlichen Hinweisen zu den koranischen Schwüren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-3:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-3:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-3:anmerkung/r2.claim: For the structure and function of this oath type, the commentary points to 93:1–2 and its parallels.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-3:anmerkung/r2.anchor: zu Aufbau und Funktion des hier vorliegenden Schwurtypus s. die Anmerkung zu 93:1.2 mit zahlreichen Parallelstellen

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-2:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-2:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-2:anmerkung/r1.claim: The night/day oath parallels other early Meccan oaths and is especially close in wording to 91:3–4; the brightening day corresponds to ḍuḥā in 91:1 and 93:1.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-2:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Insbesondere zu 91:3.4 (wa-n-nahāri ʾiḏā ǧallāhā / wa-l-laili ʾiḏā yaġšāhā) besteht eine enge sprachliche Verwandtschaft

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r1.claim: Night/day and male/female form two cosmic oppositions; the second oath enigmatically points to God, who speaks explicitly in the first-person plural in verses 7–10.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r1.anchor: Der einleitende Schwurabschnitt nennt zwei umfassende kosmische Gegensatzpaare

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r2.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r2.claim: Neuwirth reads the two elemental pairs as the structural matrix for differing human aims and their corresponding recompense.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r2.anchor: die wiederum gegensätzliche Arten der Vergeltung nach sich ziehen.“ (Neuwirth, „Horizont“, 24)

TABATABAI:92:2-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:2-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:2-7/r2.claim: The night swallows the day, as in 13:3; it may instead be understood as covering earth or sun.
TABATABAI:92:2-7/r2.anchor: إقسام بالليل إذا يغشى النهار على حد قوله تعالى يغشي الليل النهار

THALABI:v10p216#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p216#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p216#3/r1.claim: Night covers the day and takes away its light.
THALABI:v10p216#3/r1.anchor: والليل إذا يغشى النهار فيذهب بضوءه

WAHIDI-QT:92:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:1/r1.claim: Night covers the horizon with its darkness.
WAHIDI-QT:92:1/r1.anchor: { والليل إذا يغشى } أي يغشى الافق بظلمته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r1.claim: Using a past verb for a present event makes it vivid and immediate; the author illustrates this with the Prophet's turning toward heaven and the reproach for killing prophets.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r1.anchor: حكاية الحال الفعل الماضي تضفي عليه الحركة والحيوية وتجعله كأنه معاصر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r2.claim: Arabic grammarians describe this vivid tense shift as transporting the listener to the event or bringing the event to the listener; past verbs have more temporal uses than the single schoolbook past.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r2.anchor: إما ينقلك إلى الحدث أو ينقل الحدث إليك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r3.claim: Contrast makes meanings clearer and more visible; in the opening oath, night covers while day becomes manifest, and the object of يغشى is omitted to keep every possible object in view.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p361/r3.anchor: المفعول لفعل يغشى محذوف فلم يقل سبحانه ماذا يغشى الليل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p362/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p362/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p362/r1.claim: Night's covering unfolds gradually, so يغشى is present tense; daylight appears at once at sunrise, so تجلى is past tense, as in the parallel verbs in al-Shams.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p362/r1.anchor: الليل يغشى شيئا فشيئا بالتدريج وهو ليس كالنهار الذي يتجلى دفعة واحدة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p410/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p410/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p410/r1.claim: Sajā brings together stillness and darkness, matching revelation's suspension and loss of light; yaghshā and yasri imply movement and therefore fit less well.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p410/r1.anchor: كلمة سجى جمعت المعاني كلها التي تدل على انقطاع الوحي وسكونه

ELMALILI:92:1/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:1/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:1/r1.claim: The opening oaths summarize the preceding surah: that surah moved from light to darkness and toward knowledge of God and self, ending with Thamud's ruin; this surah moves from annihilation toward witnessed light, purification, growth, and abiding in God.
ELMALILI:92:1/r1.anchor: fenâdan nûr-ı şuhûda doğru tecellî, tezekkî ve nemâ ile bekā-billâha gidilecek

ELMALILI:92:1/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:1/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:1/r2.claim: The previous surah ended with a warning, while this one begins in warning and proceeds toward glad tidings; destruction of a people or world does not diminish the Creator, who can renew creation with day, male, and female.
ELMALILI:92:1/r2.anchor: Bir kavmin ve hatta bütün âlemin helâk ve fenasıyla Hâlık’a bir eksiklik, bir ziyan gelmez, O’nun kudretine bir tevakkuf ârız olmaz.

ELMALILI:92:1/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:1/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:1/r3.claim: Night signifies cosmic and inward darkness; its definite article may refer to the whole kind of night or to a particular terrifying night, literally or figuratively.
ELMALILI:92:1/r3.anchor: “leyl”in lâmı cinse masruf olarak gece cinsinin böyle bir lahzasına veya ahde mahmul olarak hakīkī ve mecâzî bütün mânasıyla

ELMALILI:92:1/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:1/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:1/r4.claim: Yaghshā can mean that darkness covers the sun, daylight, all the horizons, grief, or the eyes, hearts, and faculties through sleep and heedlessness.
ELMALILI:92:1/r4.anchor: karanlığıyla Güneş’i veya gündüzü veya örtebileceği her şeyi ile âfâkı ve hatta gam u kasveti

ELMALILI:92:1/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:1/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:1/r5.claim: The encompassing night can carry a person from differentiation to unity, multiplicity to solitude, and witnessing to annihilation in an overwhelming immersion.
ELMALILI:92:1/r5.anchor: insanı farktan cem‘e, kesretten halvete, şuhuddan fenâya götürmek üzere

ELMALILI:92:1/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:1/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:1/r6.claim: Omitting the object of covering broadens the meaning and heightens terror; the wording also points back to the night covering the sun in the previous surah.
ELMALILI:92:1/r6.anchor: Bununla evvelki sûredeki وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰهَا’ya [eş-Şems 91/4] işaret edilmiş olmakla beraber mef‘ûlün hazfinde daha ziyade bir ta‘mîm ve ibham ile tehvil vardır.

ELMALILI:92:1/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:1/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:1/r7.claim: The conditional idhā asserts realization and, because the imperfect can indicate present or future, signals that the event may occur now or later.
ELMALILI:92:1/r7.anchor: اِذَا tahakkuk ifade etmek ve muzâri‘hâl ve istikbâle muhtemil olmak

ELMALILI:92:1/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:1/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:1/r8.claim: The image can warn of a town or people being engulfed by punishment, the era of ignorance around the Prophet's mission, death agonies, or resurrection events.
ELMALILI:92:1/r8.anchor: bâhusus bi‘set-i seniyye sıralarında dünyayı sarmış bulunan devr-i cehalet hâline ve istikbâle ait olmak üzere de sekerât-ı mevt veya kıyamet ahvâline

ELMALILI:92:1/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:1/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:1/r9.claim: Night here is the accidental darkness of passing-away after existence, not primordial nonexistence; at this moment the verses declare that all perishes except God's face, and readers pass from annihilation to abiding witness.
ELMALILI:92:1/r9.anchor: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍۢ وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلْجَلَٰلِ وَٱلْإِكْرَامِ [er-Rahmân 55/26-27] ve كُلُّ شَىْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُۥ [el-Kasas 28/88]

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r17.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r17.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf for a cloak and ten uqiyyas, after which the opening of this surah was revealed.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r17.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan tahric etmişlerdir, demiş ki

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:1/r1.claim: These oaths show the worth of the created things and the greatness of their Creator, while directing attention to the coming subject.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:1/r1.anchor: Bu yeminler de üzerine yemin edilen varlıkların değerini, onları yaratan gücün büyüklüğünü göstermekte; ayrıca gelecek konunun önemine dikkat çekmektedir

TABATABAI:92:20-21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r6.speaker: محمد بن مسلم
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r6.claim: Asked about divine oaths by created things, Imam al-Baqir answered that God may swear by any of His creatures, while creatures may swear only by God.
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن مسلم قال قلت لأبي جعفر عليه السلام قول الله عز وجل

TABATABAI:92:20-21/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r7.speaker: علي بن مهزيار
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r7.claim: Al-Faqih also transmits the ruling that God may swear by His creation but creatures may swear only by Him, through Ali ibn Mahziyar from Imam al-Baqir II.
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r7.anchor: ورواه في الفقيه بإسناده عن علي بن مهزيار عن أبي جعفر الثاني

TABATABAI:92:20-21/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r8.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r8.claim: In al-Qummi’s gloss, the night covers the day, and the phrase is an oath.
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r8.anchor: قال حين يغشى النهار وهو قسم

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p364/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p364/r1.speaker: النبي وعلي بن أبي طالب وابن مسعود وأبو الدرداء وابن عباس
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p364/r1.claim: The Prophet, ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Abū al-Dardāʾ, and Ibn ʿAbbās are reported reading ‘the male and the female’ without ما; Ibn Jinnī treats this as evidence for a variant that makes the pair genitive as an appositive to ما.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p364/r1.anchor: قرأ: "والنهار إذا تجلى والذكر والأنثى" بغير "ما1" - النبي "صلى الله عليه وسلم"

ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r2.claim: The Night is unanimously counted as twenty-one verses; most say it is Meccan, while ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa says Medinan and others divide it between the two settings.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r2.anchor: لا خلاف في أنها إحدى وعشرون آية واختلف في مكيتها ومدنيتها فالجمهور على أنها مكية وقال علي بن أبي طلحة مدنية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r3.claim: Most reports say the surah was revealed about Abū Bakr, with sound chains from Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and others; al-Suddī instead links it to Abū al-Daḥdāḥ's charitable purchase of a palm for orphans, but that Ibn ʿAbbās report is weak according to al-Suyūṭī.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r3.anchor: فالجمهور على أنها نزلت في شأن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه وروي ذلك بأسانيد صحيحة عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وغيرهما
